title: Skill: planning rules for vocabularies, deletions, repairs and cross-repo ticks
description:
Four general planning rules learned in ticfac runs, absent from the skill's pre-run review and tick-patterns.md:

1. A tick that DECLARES a vocabulary (enum, schema, table) and one that CONSUMES it go in different waves — same-wave pairs died on add/add conflicts.
2. A deletion tick first LISTS every effect the deleted path produced (events, bounds, logs, schedules) and names each one's new owner or records it as dropped; that list is its acceptance, not 'tests still pass'. (One deletion silently dropped four effects, found one finding at a time.)
3. A repair tick for a defect that is a SHAPE names every implementation of the seam (grep across languages/executors), leaves a guard test, and proves the fix by reproducing on the old code — one-site repairs took three ticks for one defect.
4. A tick lives where its CODE is: a change to another repository is a tick filed in that repository, never a child in this one (a cross-repo child was undispatchable across seven dispatches).
acceptance_criteria: Each of the four rules appears in tick-patterns.md with a one-line why, and the SKILL.md pre-run review checklist references the relevant ones (waves, deletion, repair, cross-repo)
